title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 4)
summary: Fourth Hagakure session on keeping the mind free of evil, self-questioning, body and spirit as puppet and puppeteer, selflessness and the way above morality. He ends with reading widely and avoiding ideological pigeonholes.
claims: Every man has demons; denying them is dangerous because you lose control when they get loose; acknowledge and keep a grip on them
Evil has three strata, existence within you, materialisation in your mind, then action; stop it at the thought stage
Dwelling on something long enough creates an environment where it happens, which is what manifestation really is
Allow no excuses: own your mistakes even when something external caused them
Diligent training, physical and spiritual and aimed at progress, differs from just training; some train 10 years with zero progress
Ask yourself whether you truly did your best; you cannot lie to your own heart, and breaking a promise to yourself is the worst
Honest self-questioning cuts through the ego's defense mechanisms and excuses
The body is the puppet and the spirit the puppeteer; both must be strong for either to matter
People with strong, developed bodies have strong spirits, and the two compete with each other for life
He believes, admittedly as bro science, that a strong spirit keeps the body resilient against sickness and injury
It is hard to love yourself in a body that is not up to par; improving the body can improve mental health tenfold
Those who build good bodies yet stay insecure usually followed someone else's path
Do good deeds anonymously and expect nothing back; staging acts of virtue is shameful
Always be sincere and true to yourself even if it hurts; people who are not lose who they are
If you cannot convince someone despite being certain, accept the difference and move on; you cannot save everyone
Nothing being objectively important means you can destroy every limitation, not that you should do nothing
As a teacher he found the most obvious concepts were the hardest for students to see
Never follow someone else's path; take what others say and make it your own, reading broadly such as every economic manifesto rather than one
Being pigeonholed into one ideology makes you easy to manipulate
Be wary of people proud of not reading; make your kids read young
Regimes that censor want you pigeonholed with only one option
